newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures jump after fresh NY rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures jump after fresh NY rally.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures took a sharp upward move on Friday in broad-based buying after New York arabica futures advanced to 17-month highs and on expectations of further New York gains.
Prices were due $40 higher at the start and rose even higher as the market triggered stop loss buying on the way up.
"London was left behind yesterday when New York spiralled and as such it had some catching up to do," said one trader.
"Some people were also getting out of their short positions," he said. "Big roasters, until now reluctant buyers, are also seen fixing their prices."
Spot March climbed to a high of $1,628 a tonne, the highest since the January 23 peak of $1,630, in brisk morning trade.
The contract finished the morning session $62 firmer at $1,616. Benchmark May was even higher, rising $73 to $1,629 but below its ceiling of $1,640.
New York coffee futures surged to 17-month highs in roller coaster dealings on Thursday, as speculators bought heavily amid bullish technical indicators and persistent supply concerns.

Prices headed lower at the opening Thursday, as the market followed through on profit-taking seen yesterday. But rumors that Procter & Gamble Co's Folgers Coffee would raise their retail coffee prices prompted some trade buying and turned the market around.
A spokeswoman at the company vehemently denied these rumors, but traders said the market's momentum had shifted anyway.
London traders Thursday's key reversal in New York -- making lower lows than the previous session while ending above its high -- was also seen as supportive.

The supply worries in New York were heightened by news a debtors' strike declared Wednesday by Colombia's independent coffee growers could support an overall trend toward lower output from the world's second-biggest coffee producer.

Traders in London said although the move would not impact supplies in the short-term, there could be some adverse implications in the longer run if creditor banks have no choice but to foreclose on mortgages and seize control of about 50,000 plantations.
In other news, major German roaster Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) announced on Friday it would raise the retail prices of its roasted coffee products by two marks per kg effective March 10.

KJS is part of the Phillip Morris Co Inc. The German market leader cited higher raw material prices for the increase. London robusta prices have risen by 30 percent since the start of the year. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
